note: customer_segment is CHAR(4), copied from CHAR(4) segment_code, so legacy values are padded to 4 characters. Spark strings never pad, so shorter codes come out without trailing spaces.
The #src temp table holds the snapshot batch. In Spark it becomes a DataFrame or a temporary view.
ISNULL takes the type of p.broker_code, which is VARCHAR(10), so 'DIRECT-SALES' (12 chars) is cut to 'DIRECT-SAL'. A Spark coalesce would write the full literal.
The product join compares VARCHAR product_code values case-insensitively, so case variants still match. A Spark join drops them, and with them the policy row, because this is an inner join.
snippet:
JOIN    stg.products pr WITH (NOLOCK)
                ON pr.product_code = p.product_code

note: The product_code join ignores trailing spaces. In Spark, a code with trailing spaces fails the inner join and the policy is lost.
snippet:
JOIN    stg.products pr WITH (NOLOCK)
                ON pr.product_code = p.product_code

note: The broker join on text matches case variants under the CI collation. A Spark binary join misses them, so broker_name is NULL.
snippet:
LEFT JOIN stg.brokers b WITH (NOLOCK)
               ON b.broker_code = p.broker_code

note: stg.brokers.broker_code is CHAR(6) and gets padded, while policy broker_code is VARCHAR(10). SQL Server ignores the padding when matching. In Spark the padded values do not match, so broker_name becomes NULL.
snippet:
LEFT JOIN stg.brokers b WITH (NOLOCK)
               ON b.broker_code = p.broker_code

note: This MERGE closes the current version of changed policies (valid_to = snapshot - 1, is_current = 'N'). Spark has to rebuild the whole dimension from its previous state and the batch.

MERGE dw.dim_policy AS tgt

note: The status <> check is case-insensitive, so a change of letter case only (e.g. 'Active' to 'ACTIVE') opens no new version in legacy. Spark would open one.
The status <> check ignores trailing spaces, so a change in trailing spaces alone does not close the version in legacy.
The status change check uses ISNULL(..., ''), so a NULL status and '' count as equal and no new version opens.
The broker_code <> check is case-insensitive, so a broker code that changes only in letter case does not trigger a new version in legacy.
The broker_code <> check ignores trailing spaces, so a code that differs only by trailing spaces does not count as a change.

The broker_code change check treats NULL and '' as the same value. Also, the source side has already been truncated to 'DIRECT-SAL' by the ISNULL at line 95, and Spark must compare against that truncated value.
ISNULL(annual_premium, 0) treats a NULL premium and 0 as equal, so that difference opens no new version.
The vehicle_reg <> check is case-insensitive, so a registration that changes only in case ('ab12cde' to 'AB12CDE') is not a change in legacy.
The vehicle_reg <> check ignores trailing spaces, so a registration with added trailing spaces is not seen as changed.
vehicle_reg is nullable. ISNULL(..., '') makes NULL and '' equal, so moving between NULL and empty opens no new version. Spark null-safe comparisons would treat it as a change.
The insert opens new current versions. The IDENTITY key policy_sk is assigned in policy_id order, continuing from the table's highest existing value, and Spark must reproduce that.
